## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

63	  const name = task?.decl?.invocation_endpoint ?? DEFAULT_ENDPOINT;
64	  const endpoints = config?.taskScheduler?.endpoints ?? {};
65	  const entry = endpoints[name];
66	  if (!entry) {
67	    return { name, error: `this repo's config declares no invocation endpoint "${name}" (taskScheduler.endpoints)` };
68	  }
69	  if (!entry.url) return { name, error: `invocation endpoint "${name}" declares no url` };
70	  if (!entry.tokenSecret) return { name, error: `invocation endpoint "${name}" declares no tokenSecret (the NAME of the repo Actions secret holding its token)` };
71	  return { name, url: entry.url, tokenEnv: entry.tokenSecret, headers: { ...DEFAULT_HEADERS, ...(entry.headers ?? {}) } };
72	}
73	
74	// The fire payload: which item, and the nonce that proves this call is the one
75	// the hand-off comment recorded. Prose, not JSON — the field is freeform and
76	// unparsed, so a structured payload would arrive as a literal string — and
77	// deliberately free of instructions, because the routine's stored prompt is what
78	// says how to act on it (see `instructions.md`). The session still validates
79	// the item in code before touching it: a payload labelled untrusted is trusted no
80	// more than a label event was.
81	export const firePayload = ({ repo, item, nonce }) =>
82	  `Claudinite work item: ${repo}#${item.number}. Invocation nonce: ${nonce}.`;
83	
84	// The invoker seam the executor calls, exactly once per item. Failure is DATA,
85	// never a throw, and it comes in two kinds the caller must treat differently:
86	//
87	//   { ok: true, sessionId, sessionUrl }   the routine fired; a session exists
88	//   { ok: false, answered: true, error }  the endpoint ANSWERED and refused —
89	//                                         no session, and the cause is a
90	//                                         configuration fault a retry cannot fix
91	//   { ok: false, answered: false, error } no answer reached us — a timeout, a
92	//                                         dropped connection. The session may or
93	//                                         may not exist, and nothing here may
94	//                                         guess which.
95	export function agentInvoker({ repo, config, env = process.env, fetchImpl = fetch, timeoutMs = 60e3 }) {
96	  return async function invoke({ task, item, nonce }) {
97	    const endpoint = resolveEndpoint(config, task);
98	    // A configuration fault, decided before any call: definite, and no session.
99	    if (endpoint.error) return { ok: false, answered: true, error: endpoint.error };
100	    const token = env[endpoint.tokenEnv];
101	    if (!token) {
102	      // The `required_secrets` posture, applied to the endpoint token: nothing
103	      // fails silently, the task just doesn't work yet, and the item names which
104	      // secret to set (DESIGN §14.7).
105	      return { ok: false, answered: true, error: `the Actions secret \`${endpoint.tokenEnv}\` for invocation endpoint "${endpoint.name}" is not set in this repo` };
106	    }
107	
108	    const payload = { text: firePayload({ repo, item, nonce }) };
109	
110	    // ONE call. No loop, and deliberately no `attempts` knob for anyone to raise.
111	    try {
112	      const res = await fetchImpl(endpoint.url, {
113	        method: 'POST',
114	        headers: {
115	          ...endpoint.headers,
116	          'content-type': 'application/json',
117	          authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
118	          'user-agent': 'claudinite-executor',
119	        },
120	        body: JSON.stringify(payload),
121	        signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs),
122	      });
123	      let json = null;
124	      try { json = await res.json(); } catch { json = null; }
125	      if (res.status >= 200 && res.status < 300) {
126	        return {
127	          ok: true,
128	          sessionId: json?.claude_code_session_id ?? null,
129	          sessionUrl: json?.claude_code_session_url ?? null,
130	        };
131	      }
132	      // A status came back, so the endpoint decided: no session was started, and
133	      // the cause is a token, a URL or a routine — none of which a retry fixes.
134	      return {
135	        ok: false, answered: true,
136	        error: `endpoint "${endpoint.name}" returned ${res.status}${json?.error ? `: ${JSON.stringify(json.error)}` : ''}`,
137	      };
138	    } catch (e) {
139	      // Nothing came back. The request may have landed and started a session, so
140	      // this is the one outcome that must never be retried and never be reported
141	      // as a failure — it is genuinely unknown, and the caller says so on the item.
142	      return { ok: false, answered: false, error: `endpoint "${endpoint.name}" gave no answer: ${e.message}` };
143	    }
144	  };
145	}

14	// first, and a zero delta pushes nothing at all (capture-log.mjs, pinned by tests).
15	//

17	// record, every miss leaves exactly the merge-only behaviour. The runner swallows a
18	// non-zero exit, so this reports honestly rather than pretending to succeed: a repo
19	// with no `origin` remote, or no transcript on disk, simply exits non-zero and the
20	// runner logs it.

22	import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
23	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# The site's build step — everything that must happen to the tree before the
# publish set is assembled. Named by `build_command` in .github/site.config, so
# the release pipeline and the pull-request gate run exactly this, and a change
# here is exercised on the PR before it can reach a deploy.
#
# These were two inline steps of the hand-rolled pages.yml the static-website
# pack replaces; the logic is unchanged and it produces the same two files.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

# The build stamp the debug pill shows: the last commit's time, in the timezone
# the festival is followed from, so "when was this built" reads the way a user
# expects rather than in UTC.
TIME=$(TZ='Asia/Jerusalem' git log -1 --date=format-local:'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M' --format=%cd)
printf 'window.__BUILD__ = { time: "%s" };\n' "$TIME" > js/build-info.js
echo "Stamped build time $TIME (Israel) into js/build-info.js"

# The Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon token, declared in site.config's build_vars
# and exported into this script's environment by the pipeline.
#
# On the pipeline the else-branch is unreachable: a declared build_var with no
# value fails the run before the build starts, precisely so a deploy can never
# publish a page whose beacon is silently dead. The branch is here for the OTHER
# caller — a local run or a fork, where the variable legitimately does not exist
# and leaving the placeholder in place (analytics no-ops) is the right outcome.
if [ -n "${CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  sed -i "s#REPLACE_WITH_CLOUDFLARE_WEB_ANALYTICS_TOKEN#${CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN}#" js/analytics.js
  echo "Injected the Cloudflare Web Analytics token from CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN."

# Fringe Planner (`/plan`)

A **desktop-oriented** planning surface for EdFringeNow, served at
`edfringenow.com/plan/`. It is deliberately separate from the mobile-first home
site ("Fringe Discover") and does **not** touch it — the home site stays as-is
until this matures.

> **Status:** Milestone 2 — *favourites → availability calendar → allocated
> itinerary*. You upload your edfringe.com favourites CSV export — or search the
> programme and star shows one at a time — and the board's body swaps the drop
> stage for the availability grid, showing each favourite as a lane across
> August. The swap is **only** that body: one card, one count line
> (*"4 shows planned out of 6 selected!"*) and one search bar, all in the same
> place in both states, so the first show you add never shunts the page.
> Scrub a date window — or let *"Pick my best dates"* place it for
> a given stay length or the best Sat–Sun weekend — to see **how many of your
> shows are actually catchable**. Those catchable shows are **instantly** slotted
> into a clash-free, day-by-day itinerary (one performance each, travel time
> between them) — no "Plan" button; it re-plans live as you drag the window or
> tune the controls (day hours, meal breaks, travel mode, per-day limits, or
> click a show name to pin it into the plan — or a day mark to pin that exact
> performance). Export as a **CSV itinerary** or an
> **ICS calendar feed**.

## 100% client-side

There is **no server and no build step**. Everything runs in the browser:

1. On load, `plan.js` fetches three files already shipped in this repo and joins
   them into the catalogue the engine consumes (`lib/hydrate.js`): the compact
   catalogue `../data/normalized/shows.min.json` (4,114 shows, each with a
   `performances[]` of `{date, start}`), the shared lookups `../data/venues.json`
   it indexes into, and `../data/normalized/availability.min.json`, which supplies
   each performance's `{soldOut, status}`.

   They are three files rather than one so each can be cached for as long as its
   contents last — 4 days for the catalogue (948 KB gzipped), 1 day for
   availability (149 KB), which is the only one of them that moves through the
   day. See
   [`shared/data-cache.js`](../shared/data-cache.js) and the caching table in
   [`scraper/README.md`](../scraper/README.md). Availability is the one fetch

   failure it is (the wrong kind of file, or last year's export) — never as
   "N favourites loaded". The board and the stored list are left untouched.
3. The availability calendar and the draggable date window recompute live via
   the pure engine in [`lib/`](lib/); the *"Pick my best dates"* control scores
   every candidate window in the browser the same way.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Pre-commit gate — runs the repo's verification suite (tests, JS/Python syntax,
# and the Claudinite conformance sweep) before a commit is created, so nothing
# red lands in history. The sweep makes this ~10s rather than ~2s; that is the
# deliberate trade for a local gate that covers what CI blocks on.
#
# Enable once per clone (tracked hooks aren't active by default):
#   git config core.hooksPath .githooks      # or: npm run setup-hooks
#
# Bypass for a genuine work-in-progress commit with:  git commit --no-verify
set -euo pipefail
exec bash "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/scripts/verify.sh"
---site.config---
# The static-website pack's keys — every repo-specific value the vendored release
# pipeline reads. Explicit on purpose: nothing here is published, versioned,
# built or tested except what this file names.
#
# The site is served from the repo root, so the publish set is the part of the
# root that IS the site. Everything else at the root is how the site is MADE:
# scraper/, docs/, design-concepts/, product-wiki/, plan/design/, scripts/ and
# the agent tooling were all served by the whole-root upload this replaces, and
# are deliberately absent here.
publish_root=.

# Named in four groups: the pages and their icons; the two front-ends' code and
# styles; the planner's own paths; and the data the browser actually fetches.
#
# The code DIRECTORIES are named as directories, not file by file, and that is a
# considered trade: a file-by-file list is exact but silently breaks the site the
# day someone adds js/foo.js and forgets this file, while a directory keeps
# working. The cost is that js/__tests__, shared/__tests__ and plan/lib/__tests__
# ride along — a few KB of harmless test code on a public site, which is the
# cheaper of the two failures.
#
# The data entries are the opposite: named file by file, because the two biggest
# files under data/ are scraper INPUTS that no page ever fetches, and shipping
# them is 10.3 MB of nothing. Excluded on purpose, verified against the fetch
# call sites in js/app.js and plan/plan.js:
#   data/normalized/shows.json  7.4M  the uncompacted master; the planner loads
#                                     shows.min.json instead
#   data/prices.json            2.9M  the scraper's price cache, already folded
#                                     into the catalogue before it ships
publish_paths=.nojekyll index.html accessibility.html privacy.html terms.html favicon.ico favicon.svg apple-touch-icon.png css js shared package.json plan/index.html plan/plan.css plan/plan.js plan/lib data/venues.json data/days data/normalized/shows.min.json data/normalized/availability.min.json data/normalized/descriptions.min.json

# package.json is the single source of truth; the debug pill fetches it to show
# the running version, which is why it is in the publish set above too.
version_files=package.json

# Stamps js/build-info.js and injects the analytics beacon token — the two inline
# steps the hand-rolled deploy did, now a script that also runs on every pull
# request instead of only on a deploy.
build_command=bash scripts/build-site.sh
